narrative:
On November 2, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 41.8%, taking up 1,130 of the 2,702 scheduled matters across 49 judges. This represents a minor decline from the 44.8% conversion rate achieved on October 30 (1,153 heard of 2,572 scheduled), yet remains stronger than earlier sessions on October 29 (37.7%) and October 28 (35.4%).

Judicial clearance exhibited significant bench-level variance. Justice S. Rachaiah logged the highest individual volume, hearing 88 of 133 matters (66.2%), while Justice T.P. Vivekananda achieved high efficiency by taking up 51 of 59 cases (86.4%). Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty handled substantial volume across two halls, hearing 114 of 193 listed cases (59.1%). In contrast, several benches saw no progress; Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard none of the 143 cases listed across his dockets, a sharp divergence from his 100% completion on lower-volume cause lists during late October. 

Procedural stages formed the core of the court's daily workload. Orders represented the single largest stage with 919 listings and a 44.9% hearing rate, slightly down from 47.3% on October 30. Matters at the Admission stage reached a 49.0% conversion rate (304 of 620 heard), improving upon the 46.6% recorded on October 30. Conversely, Final Hearings experienced persistent clearance bottlenecks, converting only 25.5% of 443 scheduled matters, consistent with historical rates hovering around 22% to 27%.

By subject classification, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated overall scheduling with 1,174 cases but cleared at a modest 37.2%. Criminal matters progressed more rapidly: Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) recorded a 50.9% hearing rate (228 of 448 heard), improving from 44.8% on October 30, while Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) reached 61.0%. Regular First Appeals (RFA) lagged noticeably, converting just 13.4% of 134 listings.
